name: pajamax (synchronous gRPC server)
baseline: tonic (rust_tonic_mt entry in grpc_bench, unary RPC)
verdict_reason: The "up to 10X faster than Tonic" claim divides requests per second by measured CPU use; in raw requests per second the author's own run peaks at 2.9x-3.0x. A third-party grpc_bench run found pajamax 3-4% ahead of tonic on 1 and 4 CPUs and 30% ahead on 24.
tier_reason: Both runs use the public grpc_bench harness with hardware and parameters stated; one run is by pajamax's author, the other by an unrelated maintainer.
claimed_speedup: Author claim: up to 10X faster than Tonic. Author run (AMD EPYC 9754, server on 1 CPU) req/s pajamax vs tonic_mt: 183167 vs 62969 at C=10/S=1000, 144842 vs 48014 at C=100/S=1000 (2.91x, 3.02x) (derived from page data). Third-party run (Ryzen 9 5900X) req/s: 1 CPU 13288 vs 12793, 4 CPUs 49806 vs 48307, 24 CPUs 249189 vs 191674 (1.04x, 1.03x, 1.30x) (derived from page data)
workload: grpc_bench unary RPC with the complex_proto request, ghz load generator; author run varies connections C (1-100) and concurrent streams S (1-100,000) with the server limited to 1 CPU; third-party run uses 100 connections and 10,000 concurrency with server and client limited to 1, 4 or 24 CPUs.
hardware: Author run: AMD EPYC 9754, 16 CPUs, 32 GB, Ubuntu 22.04. Third-party run: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, Ubuntu 24.04.
toolchain: Per grpc_bench Dockerfiles; not stated in the results.
platforms: Not stated; benchmarked on Linux x86_64
one_liner: Thread-per-connection gRPC server with a gRPC-specific HTTP/2 parser; 3-30% faster than tonic in a third-party run, not the 10x its author cites.
how_it_is_fast: Each connection gets its own OS thread running synchronous code, so there is no async runtime between the socket and the handler. Its HTTP/2 layer is written for gRPC only: it ignores headers other than :path and handles :path without allocating an owned String. Many streams on one connection let one read syscall carry many requests.
use_it_when: Internal unary-only gRPC services behind a gateway, with few long-lived connections carrying many concurrent streams.
skip_it_when: You need streaming RPCs or gRPC headers such as grpc-timeout; pajamax supports unary calls only.
The server faces many short-lived connections from the internet; one thread per connection does not scale there.
caveats: The 10x figure is req/s per CPU, and the CPU readings for pajamax are implausibly low in places (10.49% CPU while serving 48,265 req/s), so the per-CPU ratio may overstate the gap.
The author run limits the server to one CPU; the third-party run that found a 3-4% gap at 1 and 4 CPUs was published by the author of a competing library (wtx).
grpc_bench marks pajamax's implementation as on hold (rust_pajamax_bench_onhold), and the maintainer's 2026-04 run does not include it.
tradeoffs: Unary RPC only; no streaming, no gRPC headers such as grpc-timeout.
Very small user base (31 GitHub stars).

evidence.quote: We measured that Pajamax is up to at most 10X faster than Tonic using
In most cases, there is a significant difference in CPU usage between Pajamax and Tonic.
